evidence: The actual workbook Quality Checks A10:D10 requires sane CPU/memory, no secret literals and public network. Its Internal Quality Checks D10 still says no-network; the public wording and frozen skill Delivery profile explicitly supersede that annotation. Frozen task/task.toml:21-24 declares build_timeout_sec=600.0, network_mode=public, cpus=2 and memory_mb=4096; these are exactly the frozen template's environment settings. There is no environment.env, docker_image or allow_internet key. Two CPUs and 4 GiB are a reasonable allocation for this local Node/Express/SQLite app and ordinary frontend build; no special heavyweight dependency is demanded (environment/instructions/integration.md:3,13). The agent Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template (SHA256 0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1). Its sole ENV is NODE_PATH at line 3; lines 14-15 copy only instructions and assets. Manual reading of every environment file found no credential literal; the empty seed is environment/assets/seed_data.json:1-4 and Dockerfile:20 uses synthetic turing@local.invalid. The token reference in task.toml:34 is a verifier-only variable placeholder, not an agent secret. Conforming alternative considered: an app that installs frontend tools or uses CDN editor/font assets is explicitly permitted by integration.md:13 and policy.md:7; security.md:9 distinguishes user-entered snippets from app assets. Broken-app consideration: a dead static app can share correct infrastructure and satisfy this environment row, but that does not establish any app grade.
